# A rank consequence of the all-active-circuit condition

This is a finite-dimensional linear-algebra lemma. Its application to depth
inherits the explicit differentiability and sharp-center hypotheses of
all-active-circuit-directional-condition.md. It is not a proof that those
hypotheses hold at an arbitrary extremizer.

## 1. Independent representatives

Let X_1,...,X_k be nonempty subsets of a finite-dimensional real vector
space. There exist linearly independent choices x_i in X_i if and only if

    dim span(union_{i in I} X_i) >= |I|

for every subset I of {1,...,k}.

Necessity is immediate. For sufficiency use induction on k; the case k=1
is immediate. If some nonempty proper I is tight, first choose independent
representatives for I. Their span equals V_I=span(union_{i in I} X_i).
In the quotient by V_I, every remaining subset J has span dimension at
least |J|, because the condition for I union J gives at least |I|+|J|
before quotienting. Induction in the quotient gives the other choices.
They and the representatives for I are independent.

If there is no nonempty proper tight subset, choose a nonzero x_k in X_k.
Every nonempty I among the first k-1 indices has span dimension at least
|I|+1; its quotient by span{x_k} has dimension at least |I|. Induction in
that quotient gives the remaining independent choices. This proves the
criterion. No convexity, compactness, or closedness of X_i is required.

## 2. Universal positive dependence forces a low-dimensional essential block

Suppose nonempty sets X_1,...,X_k satisfy

    0 belongs to conv{x_1,...,x_k} for EVERY choice x_i in X_i.       (U)

Choose an inclusion-minimal nonempty index set I for which (U) holds with
only those indices. Then

    dim span(union_{i in I} X_i) <= |I|-1.                         (R)

Proof. Work only with the minimal set I, relabeling it {1,...,r}. Every
representative system is linearly dependent by (U). The preceding criterion
therefore gives a nonempty J with positive deficiency

    D(J)=|J|-dim V_J > 0,
    V_J=span(union_{j in J} X_j).

Choose J maximizing D(J) among all subsets. For every L in the complement,
maximality implies

    dim(V_J+V_L)-dim V_J >= |L|.

The independent-representatives criterion in the quotient by V_J therefore
chooses one representative x_l from each outside set, with their quotient
vectors linearly independent. Fix these outside representatives. For ANY
choices x_j in the sets indexed by J, property (U) gives nonnegative
coefficients summing to one whose weighted representative sum is zero.
Project to the quotient by V_J. Independence forces every coefficient of
an outside representative to vanish. Hence zero belongs to the convex hull
of the chosen representatives from J alone. This holds for every choice
inside J. Minimality of I forces J=I, and positive deficiency gives (R).

Zero vectors and singleton zero sets cause no exception: a singleton zero
set itself gives an essential block of dimension zero.

## 3. Conditional application to depth extrema

In the notation of candidate 6a6bd3b533ab6973, suppose a
true local minimum in an open body-parameter space satisfies that note's
hypotheses. For each deepest integer index z, let Gamma_z be the compact
convex set of ALL balanced active-circuit gradients after subtracting
beta times the total-volume gradient. Its necessary condition is

    0 in conv{g_z : z deepest} for EVERY choice g_z in Gamma_z.

There is consequently an essential nonempty subset I of deepest indices
whose entire collection of circuit gradients spans a space of dimension
at most |I|-1. Equivalently, on a linear subspace of parameter variations
of codimension at most |I|-1, EVERY active circuit at EVERY site in I has
exactly the normalized total-volume derivative.

This is stronger than obtaining one balancing relation after selecting one
circuit at each site. For a unique essential deepest site, all of its circuit
gradients are identically zero. It does not by itself bound |I| by 2^n, rule
out a stationary family, or give the required numerical constant. Those
would require additional geometric input.
